title: The Definition of a Function and Its Vocabulary
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Explain in your own words what a function is, and clearly distinguish the domain, codomain, and range. What does the uniqueness requirement forbid?
finalAnswer: A function $f: D \to C$ is a rule that assigns each input $x \in D$ exactly one output $f(x) \in C$; the range $\{f(x) : x \in D\}$ is the set of outputs actually produced.

steps.title: State the Core Idea
steps.explanation: A function is a rule that takes each element of a starting set D and produces an element of a target set C. The machine metaphor works well: one input goes in, exactly one output comes out.
steps.why: Every review answer about functions must anchor on the input-output rule first.

steps.title: Separate Domain, Codomain, and Range
steps.explanation: The domain is the set of permitted inputs, the codomain is the set of declared possible outputs, and the range is the subset of the codomain the function actually hits. For f(x) = x^2 with domain and codomain all real numbers, the range is only [0, infinity).
steps.why: Students often confuse codomain with range; a concrete example keeps them apart.

steps.title: Enforce the Uniqueness Requirement
steps.explanation: Each input must have exactly one output. Different inputs are allowed to share the same output (x^2 sends both 3 and -3 to 9), but a single input claiming two different values, such as a rule sending 1 to both 2 and 5, is not a function.
steps.why: Uniqueness of the output per input is precisely the property the Vertical Line Test later checks geometrically.
